def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $s\ge0$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty open set. Use $H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ with the Bessel-potential completion convention of [[def-real-order-bessel-potential-sobolev-space]]. Define the **restriction space**
$$H^s(D):=\{U|_D:U\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)\},\qquad \|u\|_{H^s(D)}:=\inf\{\|U\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^d)}:U|_D=u\text{ a.e. on }D\}.$$
Two extensions represent the same element exactly when their restrictions agree almost everywhere on $D$. This is the convention for fractional-order spaces on the polyhedral domain and its affine simplex cells used in the Nitsche items on this page. No $C^1$ boundary or trace theorem is part of this definition.
lem-nitsche-h-one-zero-functions-have-ze:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ have a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and let $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)=W^{1,2}_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ have the closure convention of [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]] and [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]. For every boundary facet $F\subset\partial K$ there is a bounded affine-simplex trace map $T_{K,F}:W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R)\to L^2(F;\mathbb R)$ agreeing with classical restriction on smooth functions. If $w\in H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, then $T_{K,F}(w|_K)=0$ in $L^2(F;\mathbb R)$. In particular, any globally $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ function that is polynomial on each cell and belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ has zero classical boundary restriction on every boundary facet.
lem-nitsche-local-polynomial-flux-invers:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge2$, a degree $k\ge1$, and a shape-regular matching affine simplicial mesh family as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. There is a selected constant $1\le C_{\mathrm{tr}}<\infty$, depending only on $d,k$ and the shape-regularity bound, such that for every cell $K$, every facet $F\subset\partial K$, and every scalar $v_h|_K\in\mathbb P_k(K)$,
$$h_F\|\partial_{n_{K,F}}v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C_{\mathrm{tr}}^2\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(K)}^2,$$
where $h_F=|K|/|F|$ and $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal of $K$ on $F$.
lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-sim:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $F$ be one of its facets, and let $s>1/2$. Restriction of smooth functions has a unique bounded extension
$$T_F:H^s(K)\longrightarrow L^2(F),\qquad \|T_Fv\|_{L^2(F)}\le C_s\|v\|_{H^s(K)},$$
where $H^s(K)$ is the restriction space of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. The constant depends only on $s$ and the Fourier normalization, not on the location or orientation of the supporting hyperplane. If $V\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ is an extension of $v$, then $T_Fv$ is the restriction to $F$ of the unique $L^2$ hyperplane trace of $V$; hence it is independent of the chosen extension.
lem-nitsche-scaled-fractional-simplex-tr:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge2$, $1/2<s\le1$, and a shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For $0<s<1$ and a scalar or vector-valued function $w$ on a cell $K$, define
$$|w|_{s,K}^2:=\int_K\int_K\frac{|w(x)-w(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{d+2s}}\,dx\,dy;$$
for $s=1$ set $|w|_{1,K}:=\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(K)}$ (componentwise for vectors). For every cell $K$, facet $F\subset\partial K$, and $w\in H^s(K)$ in the restriction convention of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]], the trace from [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]] satisfies
$$\|T_Fw\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C\bigl(h_K^{-1}\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K^{2s-1}|w|_{s,K}^2\bigr).$$
For $0<s<1$, the norm $\bigl(\|w\|_{L^2(K)}^2+|w|_{s,K}^2\bigr)^{1/2}$ is equivalent on a fixed reference simplex to the restriction $H^s$ norm. At $s=1$ the displayed estimate is the weak $H^1$ trace inequality; no additional identification of the full intrinsic weak-$H^1$ space with a restriction space is asserted. Constants are uniform over the shape-regular family and depend only on $d,s$ and its shape bound.

For every $w\in H^s(K)$, with cell mean $w_K:=|K|^{-1}\int_Kw$, the same conventions give
$$\|w-w_K\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K^s|w|_{s,K}.$$
def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected polyhedral open set, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of $\Omega$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. Fix a polynomial degree $k\ge1$. Let $V_h$ be the real scalar conforming polynomial space of [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]], viewed as a subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]], and let $Y_h:=V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, where $H^1_0$ is the closure convention of [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]; [[lem-nitsche-h-one-zero-functions-have-zero-facet-traces]] proves its facet-trace consequence. Boundary facets form $\mathcal F_h^\partial$. If $F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial$, let $K_F$ be its unique incident cell, $n_F$ its outward unit normal, $|F|$ its $(d-1)$-dimensional measure, and set $h_F:=|K_F|/|F|>0$. For functions with a defined boundary normal trace write $\partial_n v:=\nabla v\cdot n_F$ on $F$.

Let $\mathcal X_h$ consist of $v\in H^1(\Omega)$ such that for every cell $K$ there is $s_K>1/2$ with $v|_K\in H^{1+s_K}(K)$. By [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]], $v$ has an $L^2(F)$ trace on each facet, and each component of $\nabla(v|_K)$ is in $H^{s_K}(K)$, hence has an $L^2(F)$ trace by the same lemma; the derivative mapping follows from $|\xi_j|\langle\xi\rangle^{s_K}\le\langle\xi\rangle^{1+s_K}$ in the Bessel-potential norm. Thus $\partial_n v$ and all displayed integrals are defined. In particular, $V_h\subseteq\mathcal X_h$ and the exact/adjoint functions in the later regularity hypotheses lie in $\mathcal X_h$. For a dimensionless penalty coefficient $\gamma_0\ge0$ and symmetry parameter $\theta\in\{0,1\}$, define the same bilinear formula on $\mathcal X_h\times\mathcal X_h$:
$$a_h^\theta(v,w):=\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F(\partial_n v)w\,dS-\theta\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_Fv(\partial_n w)\,dS+\gamma_0\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\int_Fvw\,dS.$$
For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ and boundary data $g$ with the displayed integrals finite, define
$$\ell_h^\theta(w_h):=\int_\Omega f w_h\,dx-\theta\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_Fg(\partial_n w_h)\,dS+\gamma_0\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\int_Fg w_h\,dS.$$
The **nonsymmetric Nitsche form** is $a_h^0$; it has the consistency flux in the trial slot only. The **symmetric Nitsche form** is $a_h^1$; it has both transposed consistency fluxes. The discrete weak-boundary problem is the standard Nitsche method when $\gamma_0>0$: it seeks $u_h\in V_h$ such that $a_h^\theta(u_h,w_h)=\ell_h^\theta(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h$. This extension makes expressions such as $a_h^\theta(u,w_h)$ and $a_h^\theta(e,\zeta-z_h)$ well-defined when the exact and adjoint functions have the stated cellwise regularity. The boundary penalty is $\gamma_0/h_F$; $h_F$ is the cell-face height divided by $d$, not the face diameter. The zero value $\gamma_0=0$ is used only for the penalty-free algebraic comparison.

The energy seminorm and the comparison seminorm used below are
$$\|v\|_{E,h}^2:=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\|v\|_{L^2(F)}^2,\qquad \|v\|_{\#,h}^2:=\|v\|_{E,h}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n v\|_{L^2(F)}^2.$$
These expressions are used only on functions for which their volume and facet traces are defined. The parameter $\theta$ fixes the sign convention; no convention based on a reciprocal small stabilization parameter is implicit.
lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the nonempty mesh hypotheses of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. Let $N_\partial$ be the maximum number of boundary facets incident to a single cell, and use the selected positive local constant $C_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge1$ from [[lem-nitsche-local-polynomial-flux-inverse-trace]]. The mesh has at least one boundary facet, so $1\le N_\partial\le d+1$ and $C_\partial:=\sqrt{N_\partial}C_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge1$. For every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_\partial\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad C_\partial:=\sqrt{N_\partial}\,C_{\mathrm{tr}}.$$
Consequently,
$$\left|\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F(\partial_n v_h)v_h\,dS\right|\le C_\partial\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F^{-1}\|v_h\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
For simplices $N_\partial\le d+1$; no sharper face-count bound is needed.
lem-nitsche-fractional-weak-green-and-fl:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nondegenerate affine simplex, let $r>1/2$, and let $q\in H^r(K;\mathbb R^d)$ in the restriction convention of [[def-nitsche-restriction-bessel-potential-sobolev-spaces]]. Suppose $\operatorname{div}q\in L^2(K)$ distributionally. Then for every $v\in H^1(K)$,
$$\int_Kq\cdot\nabla v\,dx+\int_K(\operatorname{div}q)v\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(T_Fq\cdot n_{K,F})T_Fv\,dS,$$
where $T_Fq$ is the fractional $L^2(F)$ trace of [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]], $T_Fv$ is the weak $H^1$ endpoint trace of [[lem-nitsche-scaled-fractional-simplex-trace]] (agreeing with the Fourier trace whenever $v$ has a restriction-space extension), and $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal. This identifies the fractional facet trace of $q$ as its weak conormal flux.

Now let $\Omega$ be a nonempty bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$, let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$ with $r>1/2$, and suppose $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ distributionally. The traces of $\nabla u$ from the two cells incident to every interior facet agree as vectors, so their outward normal fluxes cancel. For every $w\in H^1(\Omega)$ the sum of the cell identities is
$$\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}\int_F\partial_nu\,T_Fw\,dS=\int_\Omega fw\,dx.$$
Here $\mathcal F_h^\partial$ is the set of boundary facets, $\partial_nu:=T_F(\nabla u)\cdot n_F$, and all interior-facet value traces of a global $H^1(\Omega)$ function agree.
thm-nitsche-zero-boundary-fractional-com:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice, $d\ge2$, a nonempty connected bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega$, a finite matching shape-regular affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$, and a polynomial degree $k\ge1$ as in [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. Put $h:=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K$ and $\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)$. For every $1/2<s\le1$ there is an explicitly defined linear map
$$I_{h,0}:H^{1+s}(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)\longrightarrow \mathbb P_1(\mathcal T_h)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)\subseteq Y_h$$
such that
$$\|\zeta-I_{h,0}\zeta\|_{\#,h}\le C h^s\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}=C_D h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad C_D:=C\ell_\Omega^{s-1}.$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_{\#,h}$ and $Y_h=V_h\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$ are exactly those of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. The constants are uniform over the mesh family and depend only on $d,s$ and its shape-regularity bound; the displayed conversion to $C_D$ uses the fixed nonempty domain. The construction uses cell means and affine reconstructions, never point values of $\zeta$. Its boundary-value error vanishes exactly. No approximation statement for higher polynomial degree or for nonzero-trace primal data is asserted.
lem-nitsche-global-fractional-boundary-f:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the fixed nonempty bounded polyhedral domain, matching shape-regular affine simplicial mesh, and Nitsche face-height convention of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]]. Let $h:=\max_Kh_K$, $\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)$, and $1/2<s\le1$. For every $\zeta\in H^{1+s}(\Omega)$, with no boundary-value or PDE assumption,
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n\zeta\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C h^{1/2}\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}=C_T h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\|\zeta\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad C_T:=C\ell_\Omega^{-1/2}.$$
The trace is the restriction of the whole-space Fourier hyperplane trace and agrees with the facet trace in [[lem-nitsche-fractional-face-trace-on-simplex]]. The constant $C_T$ may depend on the fixed domain, $d$, $s$, and the Fourier normalization, but not on the mesh.
lem-nitsche-penalty-coercivity:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] and [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]]. Put $C_\partial$ as in the latter item and let $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. If
$$\gamma_0>\frac{(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2}{4},$$
then for every $v_h\in V_h$,
$$a_h^\theta(v_h,v_h)\ge\lambda_\theta\|v_h\|_{E,h}^2,\qquad \lambda_\theta:=\frac{1+\gamma_0-\sqrt{(1-\gamma_0)^2+(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2}}{2}>0.$$
Thus the sufficient threshold is $C_\partial^2/4$ for the nonsymmetric form and $C_\partial^2$ for the symmetric form. These are thresholds certified by the displayed inverse-trace bound, not asserted to be necessary for each individual mesh.
thm-nitsche-consistency-and-energy-quasi:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the Poisson/Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] on a connected bounded polyhedral $\Omega$. Let $u\in H^{1+r}(\Omega)$, $r>1/2$, solve $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ with Dirichlet trace $g$, and let $u_h^\theta$ solve the discrete problem for $\theta\in\{0,1\}$. Use the comparison seminorm $\|\cdot\|_{\#,h}$ of the definition. Put $C_\partial$ as in [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]], and assume
$$\gamma_0>(1+\theta)^2C_\partial^2/4.$$
The discrete solution exists uniquely, and
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{\#,h},\qquad C_\theta:=1+\frac{(2+\theta C_\partial+\gamma_0)(1+C_\partial^2)}{\lambda_\theta},$$
where $\lambda_\theta$ is the positive coercivity constant in [[lem-nitsche-penalty-coercivity]]. If, in addition, the Nitsche comparison-norm approximation bound [A2] holds with exponent $t>0$, then
$$\|u-u_h^\theta\|_{\#,h}\le C_\theta C_I\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K^{2t}\|u\|_{H^{1+t}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The result keeps the weak Dirichlet trace unconstrained in $V_h$.
thm-nonsymmetric-nitsche-l2-error-with-b:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the nonsymmetric Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] and [[thm-nitsche-consistency-and-energy-quasioptimality]] with penalty above its coercivity threshold. Put $e:=u-u_h^0\in L^2(\Omega)$, and let $\zeta_e\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ solve $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla\zeta_e=\int_\Omega ve$ for all $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Let $s\in(1/2,1]$ and assume the genuine dual regularity hypothesis [A1]. The proved comparison interpolation theorem supplies $z_h:=I_{h,0}\zeta_e\in Y_h$ with $\|\zeta_e-z_h\|_{\#,h}\le C_D h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}}$, and the proved weighted flux trace theorem supplies
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n\zeta_e\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_T h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad 0<h\le\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega).$$
Then
$$\|e\|_2\le\left(M_0C_DC_Rh^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}+C_TC_Rh^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\right)\|e\|_{\#,h},$$
where $M_0:=2+\gamma_0\ge1$ and $C_D,C_T$ are mesh-uniform for the fixed domain. Since $s>1/2$ and $h\le\ell_\Omega$, the right side is $O(h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2})\|e\|_{\#,h}$ after absorbing the fixed constants. The surviving boundary term prevents claiming the symmetric $h^s$ factor from dual regularity alone.
thm-symmetric-nitsche-l2-error-under-dua:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the symmetric Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] and [[thm-nitsche-consistency-and-energy-quasioptimality]] with penalty above the symmetric coercivity threshold. Let $e:=u-u_h^1\in L^2(\Omega)$ and let $\zeta_e\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ solve the adjoint Poisson problem $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla\zeta_e\,dx=\int_\Omega ve\,dx$ for every $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Assume its dual regularity bound [A1]
$$\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}\le C_R\|e\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad s\in(1/2,1],$$
The proved interpolation theorem [[thm-nitsche-zero-boundary-fractional-comparison-interpolation]] supplies $z_h:=I_{h,0}\zeta_e\in Y_h$ and a mesh-uniform constant $C_D$ with
$$\|\zeta_e-z_h\|_{\#,h}\le C_D h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad 0<h\le\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega).$$
Set $C_\partial$ as in [[lem-nitsche-global-boundary-flux-bound]] and preserve the original constant $M_1:=2+C_\partial+\gamma_0$. Then
$$\|u-u_h^1\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le M_1 C_D C_R h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|u-u_h^1\|_{\#,h},$$
where the all-comparison-space symmetric form bound with this same $M_1$ is proved below. The dual elliptic regularity estimate remains an explicit PDE hypothesis. If, in addition, the general higher-order/local primal energy approximation hypothesis [A3] holds with exponent $t>0$, then
$$\|u-u_h^1\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le M_1 C_D C_R C_\theta C_I h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K^{2t}\|u\|_{H^{1+t}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The primal branch retains its full exponent range and local broken-norm hypothesis; the zero-boundary P1 interpolation theorem supplies the dual approximation and does not replace that branch.
